content: Despite the significant progress and financial investments observed between 2020 and 2024, the deployment of comprehensive communication infrastructure in South Africa is not without its systemic challenges. Broader discussions around the infrastructure challenges across the African continent underscore the importance of governmental reforms and execution to bolster large-scale infrastructure projects [33] . Operational complexity and security concerns surrounding network infrastructure continue to test the industry’s readiness for fully interconnected systems [33] . The transition from legacy communication systems to advanced, interoperable networks requires meticulous planning to mitigate cybersecurity risks and ensure data integrity. Furthermore, while wireless connectivity solutions like private 5G have been transformative, expansive adoption in recent years has accelerated the pace of digital integration faster than initial projections from 2020 might have anticipated [32] [35] . For entities operating within the South African market, understanding these dual infrastructure requirements—expansive, high-bandwidth coverage for surface operations and highly resilient, penetrative networks for underground environments—is paramount. The unpredictable nature of mining inherently carries risks of seismic events, structural collapses, fires, and hazardous gas leaks, necessitating communication architectures that can function flawlessly under catastrophic conditions. Despite the clear advancements in both dispatch and emergency communication technologies, the South African mining sector continues to face ongoing challenges related to full site coverage and system interoperability. Complementing the efforts of ICASA, the national government has also articulated new strategic priorities to resolve municipal-level deployment challenges. In June 2026, Communications Minister Solly Malatsi introduced a new policy direction specifically intended to unblock municipal broadband roll-out [125] . This initiative signals a robust high-level commitment to addressing the persistent inefficiencies and bureaucratic bottlenecks that have historically plagued the deployment of municipal fibre-optic networks [125] . By mandating greater cooperation between national telecom policies and local municipal administrations, this policy direction aims to create a more cohesive and supportive environment for infrastructure investments.
